Shared a table while lunching at a restaurant today, and I got talking with an older man than me (imagine!) about some of the courtesies of society in Canada, some are gone and some still happen.

One thing that reminded me of old times was how we used to watch at night for cars coming the other way and lower our headlight beams before they appeared. I can still remember going uphill and seeing the other car dim their lights before they came into view. I still do that in the country, but city life is just brighter all around.

Since I recently got a motorcycle, I've become part of a tradition that motorcycle riders wave to each other when passing in the opposite direction. It's fun, and gives a little human contact that I enjoy.

Can you think of things like this that we all used to do, or still do, for each other, on the road or elsewhere?
Remembering social conventions from a gentler time

Actually, what you describe is one of those things that I consider part of gentler times. Just the ability to start a conversation with someone randomly in a social setting without being made to feel like you might be intruding.

Thank you, I agree. Sorry it's taken days to reply, I just noticed the mail symbol. I find I have what I call "tides" in my life where my introvert self steps back a little, and such conversations are more freely available to me. Then I'll get all insular again for a while, and suddenly notice I'm missing my fellow man. Someone observed years ago to me, "If you're not having an interesting life, you're probably not paying attention!" -and that's certainly part of it for me. I'm winding up to start conversations in the coffee lineup, feel a 'tide' coming on.

Well thank you for wondering! You've given me a chuckle; making me think about it, then the voice inside said, "It's coming in and going out at the same time"... I keep seeing people around town who I know "from somewhere" but I can't place them- then it occurs to me that I've probably eaten at their restaurant, or bought something at their till...I live in a small town, but I guess it isn't that small anymore.

The hot weather with low humidity here gives me a chance to really enjoy my motorcycle...the air is all kinds of different, from one second to the next. How about your tides? Hmm. Maybe not the right question for a woman...but, you know what I mean...(grin)

Do you actually say 'hello' to these people? or just talk to yourself about who they are and where you met? :)

I've been missing motorcycle rides. Sometimes I have this urge to go up to a random stranger with a hot bike and ask for a ride. Then, I figure it's probably not the safest choice. The tides here are weird. And, not talking about 'those' tides either.

I have tried saying 'hello', usually "Hello, I know I know you from somewhere but I can't place you..." and then they tell me with mild irritation that I probably buy paint from them, or I don't know, ice cream. Or they think I'm trying to pick them up. (Maybe I am, and I haven't thought about it...there's lots I don't tell myself) You know? And then I feel a bit dumb because though I'm interested enough to know their faces, I'm really just one of the crowd; and those people who sell things and have familiar faces, have heard this before.

Reminds me of an old joke from Mad Magazine: Dental patient says, "What's the matter, Doc, you're looking down in the mouth!" and the dentist chuckles and says, "What a funny guy. That's the first time I've heard that joke...(shouting hoarsely) TODAY!!"

What are weird tides? Do you live where things are unsettled? I have to admit I'm grateful that where I am, semi-rural western Canada, there isn't a lot of strife, at least on the surface. So I worry a bit for the souls in less settled places. Hope I don't live long enough to find out what it's like.

I have to say, I'd be pleased and complimented if somebody asked for a ride; but, I don't carry a second helmet, and I don't have a lot of experience with a rider, so I'd be asking you how much You know about riding...
